data.name: AboutGhibliPreviewText
data.value: Studio Ghibli is a renowned Japanese animation studio, known for its poetic, visually striking, and emotionally profound films. Founded in 1985 by animation masters Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata, with production by Toshio Suzuki and financial support from Yasuyoshi Tokuma, the studio quickly became a global reference in auteur animation. Its works blend human themes, nature, fantasy, and social commentary, resonating with generations around the world.

data.name: SpiritedAwayPreviewDescription
data.value: A young girl enters a magical world ruled by gods, witches, and spirits, and must save her parents in this Oscar-winning masterpiece.

data.name: TheBoyAndTheHeronPreviewDescription
data.value: A boy grieving his mother discovers a hidden world guided by a mysterious heron, in Hayao Miyazaki’s Academy Award–winning tale of loss and wonder.

data.name: GraveOfTheFirefliesPreviewDescription
data.value: Two siblings struggle to survive amidst war-torn Japan, in this heartbreaking and critically acclaimed masterpiece.

data.name: PrincessMononokePreviewDescription
data.value: A warrior cursed by a deadly spirit is drawn into a fierce struggle between humans and the gods of the forest in this award-winning epic.

data.name: MyNeighborTotoroPreviewDescription
data.value: Two sisters move to the countryside and encounter gentle forest spirits, in this beloved and enchanting Studio Ghibli classic.

data.name: AboutSectionMeText
data.value: .NET developer focused on ASP.NET Core, Blazor, and clean architectures, passionate about turning ideas into well-structured, reliable digital experiences. I have hands-on experience with professional, academic and personal projects covering both back-end and front-end development, always emphasizing good practices, organization, and usability. I’m continuously expanding my skills by exploring technologies like .NET MAUI, React, Azure, and databases such as SQL Server and MySQL. Beyond technical proficiency, I value intuitive design, clear communication, and delivering solutions that combine performance and visual refinement.

data.name: AboutSectionProjectText
data.value: Front-end project developed with Blazor Server, designed to enhance practical skills and serve as a professional portfolio piece. The application explores UI/UX design principles, emphasizing clean structure, component reusability, and full responsiveness. Inspired by the magical universe of Studio Ghibli’s films, the project aims to capture the studio’s distinctive atmosphere and visual storytelling through a smooth, elegant, and user-friendly interface — blending minimalist design with cosiness.

data.name: HistoryIntro1
data.value: Founded in 1985 by Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata, together with producer Toshio Suzuki, Studio Ghibli quickly became one of the most influential animation studios in the world. Its films blend visual beauty, emotion and social reflection in a way that continues to inspire audiences of all ages.

data.name: HistoryIntro2
data.value: Below, you'll find a timeline tracing the studio's journey, from the years before it existed, when its founders were young animators learning the trade, to the worldwide acclaim that came later.

data.name: History_Era3_Title
data.value: Nausicaä and a studio of their own

data.name: History_TakahataBorn_Text
data.value: Isao Takahata is born on October 29 in Ujiyamada, in Mie Prefecture, and spends his childhood in Okayama. Of the two future founders he is the elder by five years, and the one who will reach animation by the longest road: through books, French poetry and cinema.

data.name: History_MiyazakiBorn_Text
data.value: Miyazaki is born on January 5 in Tokyo. His family runs Miyazaki Airplane, a company that makes parts for fighter planes during the war, and the boy grows up surrounded by drawings of aircraft. That fascination with flight, and the discomfort of knowing what those planes were built for, will run through almost everything he makes.

data.name: History_Okayama_Text
data.value: On June 29, American bombers set Okayama on fire. Nine-year-old Takahata runs through the streets in his pajamas with one of his sisters, separated from the rest of the family. More than forty years later, that night will reach the screen in Grave of the Fireflies.

data.name: History_Mother_Text
data.value: Miyazaki's mother is diagnosed with spinal tuberculosis and spends years between hospitals and a bed at home. She was sharp, skeptical and strong-willed, and her son would later say she shaped the way he saw the world. Her illness is the quiet heart of My Neighbor Totoro.

data.name: History_Hakujaden_Title
data.value: Falling for The Tale of the White Serpent

data.name: History_Hakujaden_Text
data.value: Toei Doga releases Hakujaden, Japan's first color animated feature. Miyazaki, a high school student cramming for university exams, watches it and falls in love, as he later admitted, with its heroine. He leaves the theater convinced that animation can carry real feeling, and a little ashamed of the imitation manga he had been drawing.

data.name: History_TakahataToei_Text
data.value: Fresh out of the University of Tokyo, where he studied French literature, Takahata joins Toei Doga as an assistant director. What drew him there was a French film, Paul Grimault's The Shepherdess and the Chimney Sweep, which showed him that animation could be poetic and political at once. He came back to that film all his life, and decades later helped bring its finished version, The King and the Mockingbird, to Japanese theaters.

data.name: History_MiyazakiToei_Text
data.value: After graduating in political science and economics from Gakushuin University, Miyazaki joins Toei Doga as an in-between animator. His first job is Watchdog Bow Wow. The pay is low and the hours are long, but he soon stands out for the ideas he keeps slipping into other people's scenes.

data.name: History_Union_Title
data.value: Side by side at the union

data.name: History_Union_Text
data.value: Miyazaki becomes chief secretary of the Toei workers' union, with Takahata as vice chairman. They had crossed paths before, but it is here, in long meetings and longer walks home, that they start talking about films, politics and what animation could still become. It is the beginning of a partnership that will last more than fifty years, often argumentative, never dull.

data.name: History_Otsuka_Text
data.value: One of Toei's first animators, Otsuka is the person who teaches both of them how movement really works and, just as important, how to have fun doing it. A lover of machines, jeeps and anything with an engine, he will be animation director on Takahata's first feature and, years later, on Miyazaki's. Neither of them ever stopped calling him a teacher.

data.name: History_Horus_Text
data.value: Takahata directs his first feature, with Miyazaki among the key animators and scene designers and Otsuka as animation director. Production drags on for three years, over schedule and over budget, and the film leaves theaters after ten days. Takahata is demoted. Today it is remembered as the moment Japanese animation started taking itself seriously.

data.name: History_Pero_Text
data.value: Miyazaki animates some of the best-remembered sequences of Toei's The Wonderful World of Puss 'n Boots, including a chase across castle rooftops that already looks like him. The film's cat, Pero, becomes Toei's mascot. The same year, under a pen name, he publishes People of the Desert, his first manga and an early sign of the storyteller he wanted to be.

data.name: History_Pippi_Title
data.value: Leaving Toei, and a Pippi that never was

data.name: History_Pippi_Text
data.value: Takahata, Miyazaki and animator Yoichi Kotabe leave Toei for A Production to adapt Pippi Longstocking. Miyazaki travels to Sweden to study the locations, but Astrid Lindgren refuses to grant the rights and the project dies. To keep working, the two take over the direction of the first Lupin III series halfway through, without credit.

data.name: History_Panda_Text
data.value: Takahata directs and Miyazaki writes and designs two short films about a little girl who lives alone and ends up adopting a baby panda and his father. The ideas left over from Pippi find a home here, and so does a big, round, gentle creature that will one day become Totoro.

data.name: History_Heidi_Text
data.value: Now at Zuiyo Eizo, the team makes Heidi, with Takahata directing and Miyazaki handling scene design and layout for all 52 episodes. They travel to Switzerland to study the light, the houses and the way people eat. That obsession with everyday life, the cooking, the chores, the weather outside, becomes a trademark of everything they do afterwards.

data.name: History_Marco_Text
data.value: Takahata directs a long, melancholy series about an Italian boy who crosses the ocean to Argentina looking for his mother, with Miyazaki again on layout. It is patient storytelling with no easy thrills, and it proves that children will follow a sad story as long as it is told honestly.

data.name: History_Conan_Text
data.value: At Nippon Animation, Miyazaki directs for the first time: a 26 episode series set after a world war, with a boy strong enough to hold his breath for ages, a girl who talks to birds and a giant flying fortress. Takahata helps with storyboards and directs a few episodes. Many ideas later seen in Castle in the Sky and Nausicaä are already here.

data.name: History_Suzuki_Text
data.value: Suzuki, a journalist at the publisher Tokuma Shoten, is on the team behind Animage, one of Japan's first magazines about animation. He calls Takahata for an interview and gets a long explanation of why Takahata will not give one. Then he goes to Miyazaki, busy on his first feature, who ignores him. Suzuki simply sits at the next desk for days until Miyazaki starts talking. They will work together for the rest of their lives.

data.name: History_Cagliostro_Text
data.value: Miyazaki leaves Takahata's Anne of Green Gables after the first episodes to make his first feature, a Lupin III adventure with Otsuka as animation director. Made in a few months, it does modest business in theaters. Years later, animators all over the world will study its car chase frame by frame.

data.name: History_Chie_Title
data.value: Chie the Brat and Gauche the Cellist

data.name: History_Chie_Text
data.value: Takahata spends the early eighties on his own projects: Chie the Brat, an Osaka comedy about a girl who runs her father's grilled offal shop, and Gauche the Cellist, a small film based on a story by Kenji Miyazawa, made over several years by a tiny studio. Both show his taste for real places, real work and music taken seriously.

data.name: History_NausicaaManga_Text
data.value: No one wants to fund an original film that isn't based on an existing work, so Suzuki suggests a way around it: make the manga first. Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind starts running in Animage. Miyazaki keeps drawing it, with long pauses whenever a film takes over his life, until 1994.

data.name: History_Tokuma_Text
data.value: The founder of Tokuma Shoten was a businessman with a gambler's instinct. He trusted Suzuki's judgment, and Suzuki trusted Miyazaki and Takahata. His money made the Nausicaä film possible and, a year later, a studio. He stayed behind Ghibli as executive producer until his death in 2000.

data.name: History_NausicaaFilm_Title
data.value: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind

data.name: History_NausicaaFilm_Text
data.value: The film opens on March 11, produced by Tokuma Shoten and the advertising agency Hakuhodo, animated at the small studio Topcraft, with Takahata as producer. It is also the first time Miyazaki works with composer Joe Hisaishi, who will score all of his films from then on. Around 900,000 people see it in theaters, enough to prove that an original story, with a girl at its center and nature as a character, could fill seats.

data.name: History_Founding_Text
data.value: On June 15, with the profits from Nausicaä and the backing of Tokuma Shoten, Miyazaki, Takahata and Suzuki open Studio Ghibli on a rented floor in Kichijoji, Tokyo, taking in part of Topcraft's staff after it closes. The name comes from a hot wind that blows across the Sahara and from an Italian airplane Miyazaki loved. The plan was to blow a new wind through Japanese animation.

data.name: History_Laputa_Text
data.value: The first film made under the Ghibli name. Miyazaki had visited Wales during the miners' strike and was moved by how those communities fought for their work, and the mining town where Pazu lives comes from there. The box office is respectable rather than spectacular, but the studio now has a direction.

data.name: History_Yanagawa_Title
data.value: A detour through the canals of Yanagawa

data.name: History_Yanagawa_Text
data.value: Takahata finishes The Story of Yanagawa's Canals, a documentary of almost three hours about a town that decided to save its old waterways, paid for with money Miyazaki had made from Nausicaä. It runs far over schedule and budget, and it is pure Takahata: curious, meticulous and in no hurry at all.

data.name: History_Totoro_Title
data.value: Totoro and the fireflies, on the same ticket

data.name: History_Totoro_Text
data.value: To get both films made, Suzuki sells them as a double feature. Audiences go from two orphans starving at the end of the war to a forest spirit waiting at a bus stop in the rain, or the other way around. Neither is a hit in theaters. Totoro finds its audience later, on television and in plush toys, and ends up becoming the studio's logo.

data.name: History_Kiki_Text
data.value: The story of a thirteen-year-old witch learning to live on her own becomes the highest grossing Japanese film of the year. With that money, Ghibli makes a choice that is rare in the industry: it hires its animators as salaried staff, raises their pay and starts training new people. From then on, the studio has to keep making films to support them.

data.name: History_OnlyYesterday_Text
data.value: Takahata tells the story of a 27-year-old office worker who spends her vacation harvesting safflower in the countryside while remembering being ten. A film for adults, about work, memory and choosing a life, it becomes the biggest Japanese hit of the year. Takahata wanted the adult faces to have cheekbones and smile lines, something anime almost never drew, and the animators sweated over every one.

data.name: History_Porco_Title
data.value: Porco Rosso, and a home of their own

data.name: History_Porco_Text
data.value: What began as a short film for Japan Airlines flights grows into a feature about a World War I pilot turned into a pig, flying seaplanes over the Adriatic. The same year, Ghibli moves into its own building in Koganei, designed by Miyazaki himself, with plenty of light and a garden on the roof.

data.name: History_OceanWaves_Text
data.value: Ghibli gives its younger staff a chance with a TV film directed by Tomomi Mochizuki, meant to be quick, cheap and good. It runs late and over budget like everything else, but it turns out to be a quiet, awkward high school story that many fans now treasure.

data.name: History_PomPoko_Text
data.value: Takahata's story of raccoon dogs fighting the construction of a new suburb on top of their forest. It is funny, full of shape-shifting and deeply sad, and one of the clearest expressions of the studio's worry about what modern Japan was doing to its land.

data.name: History_Whisper_Text
data.value: For the first time, a Ghibli feature is directed by someone other than its founders: Yoshifumi Kondo, the animator many saw as the natural successor. Written by Miyazaki, it follows a girl who wants to write and a boy who wants to make violins. Kondo died in 1998, at 47, and this remains his only film as director.

data.name: History_Disney_Text
data.value: Tokuma Shoten signs an agreement with Disney to distribute Ghibli films outside Japan. The studio's condition, repeated by Suzuki at every meeting, is simple: no cuts.

data.name: History_Mononoke_Text
data.value: Miyazaki's most ambitious film yet: a violent, morally tangled fight between an iron town, the gods of the forest and a young prince carrying a curse. Some shots use digital tools for the first time at the studio. It becomes the highest grossing film in Japanese history, until Titanic arrives a few months later. Miyazaki announces he is retiring. It will not be the last time.

data.name: History_Yamadas_Text
data.value: Takahata turns a newspaper comic strip into a string of sketches about an ordinary, slightly chaotic family, drawn like watercolors. It is the first Ghibli film made entirely on computers, and one of the most laborious, all to look as light as a doodle. The box office disappoints. Takahata will not direct again for fourteen years.

data.name: History_SpiritedAway_Text
data.value: The story of Chihiro, a sulky ten-year-old who has to work in a bathhouse for spirits to save her parents, opens in Japan and stays in theaters for months. It becomes the highest grossing film in the country's history, a record it holds for almost twenty years. It wins the Golden Bear in Berlin and, in 2003, the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. Miyazaki skips the ceremony, unwilling to visit a country that was at war in Iraq.

data.name: History_Museum_Text
data.value: The museum opens in Mitaka, built from Miyazaki's sketches, with no fixed route, spiral staircases, a giant Catbus for children to climb and a robot soldier from Castle in the Sky standing in the garden on the roof. Its motto invites visitors to get lost, together.

data.name: History_CatReturns_Text
data.value: Directed by Hiroyuki Morita, it brings back the Baron from Whisper of the Heart in a lighter adventure about a schoolgirl who saves a cat and gets dragged into its kingdom. It began as a small commission for a theme park and grew into a feature.

data.name: History_Howl_Text
data.value: Based on Diana Wynne Jones's novel, it lands in Miyazaki's hands after Mamoru Hosoda leaves the project. Made while the Iraq war was on the news every night, it turns a book about a curse into a film about the absurdity of war, and about an eighteen-year-old girl who seems happier as an old woman.

data.name: History_Independence_Text
data.value: Ghibli becomes independent from Tokuma Shoten, with Suzuki as its president. In September, Miyazaki receives the Golden Lion for lifetime achievement at the Venice Film Festival.

data.name: History_Earthsea_Text
data.value: Goro Miyazaki, Hayao's son, a landscape designer who had been running the Ghibli Museum, directs his first film, based on Ursula K. Le Guin's books. His father is against the idea, and the two barely speak during production. The film divides audiences, and Le Guin herself makes it clear she was not won over.

data.name: History_Ponyo_Text
data.value: A fish girl who wants to become human, drawn almost entirely by hand as a deliberate answer to the digital age. The waves alone look like living creatures. The film needed more than 170,000 drawings, a record for the studio.

data.name: History_Arrietty_Text
data.value: Hiromasa Yonebayashi, an animator who grew up inside the studio, directs his first film, from Mary Norton's The Borrowers, with a script by Miyazaki. A family of tiny people living under the floor of a country house, where a drop of water is heavy and a kitchen is a mountain range.

data.name: History_PoppyHill_Text
data.value: Goro Miyazaki's second film, a story about students in 1963 Yokohama trying to save their old clubhouse from demolition. The final months of production collide with the earthquake and tsunami of March 11, and the team keeps working through rolling blackouts to finish on time.

data.name: History_WindRises_Text
data.value: Miyazaki's most personal film, a portrait of Jiro Horikoshi, the engineer who designed the Zero fighter, the same kind of plane his father's company once made parts for. It asks whether you can love something beautiful knowing it will be used to kill. Jiro is voiced by Hideaki Anno, creator of Evangelion and once a young animator on Nausicaä. In September, Miyazaki announces, once again, that he is retiring.

data.name: History_Kaguya_Title
data.value: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya

data.name: History_Kaguya_Text
data.value: Takahata's farewell, eight years in the making, drawn in charcoal and watercolor lines that look unfinished on purpose. It retells Japan's oldest folktale, about a girl from the moon who wants, above everything else, to live. It is nominated for the Oscar.

data.name: History_Marnie_Title
data.value: When Marnie Was There, and a pause

data.name: History_Marnie_Text
data.value: Yonebayashi's second film, about a lonely girl and a mysterious friend in an old mansion by a marsh. Shortly after, Suzuki announces a pause in production and the animation department is dissolved. For the first time in almost thirty years, nobody is drawing a feature at Ghibli. In November, Miyazaki receives an honorary Oscar.

data.name: History_RedTurtle_Text
data.value: A co-production with the Dutch director Michaël Dudok de Wit: a film without dialogue about a man shipwrecked on an island. It wins a special prize at Cannes and shows that the studio, even on pause, still knows how to open its doors to other voices.

data.name: History_Return_Text
data.value: At 76, Miyazaki starts a new feature, and Ghibli begins hiring animators again. According to Suzuki, he is making it for his grandson, as a way of telling him that his grandfather is moving on to the next world, but leaving this film behind.

data.name: History_TakahataDies_Text
data.value: Isao Takahata dies on April 5, at 82. At the farewell held at the Ghibli Museum, Miyazaki, his voice breaking, remembers the first time he saw him: a rainy evening in 1963, at a bus stop, a young man with a gentle, intelligent face walking toward him. He calls him Paku-san, the nickname from their Toei years.

data.name: History_Earwig_Text
data.value: Goro Miyazaki directs Ghibli's first fully 3D film, based on the last book by Diana Wynne Jones, author of Howl's Moving Castle. It premieres on Japanese television at the end of the year, in the middle of the pandemic.

data.name: History_Park_Text
data.value: In Aichi Prefecture, Ghibli Park opens inside the grounds of the 2005 World Expo. There are no rides. Instead, visitors walk into the places from the films, like Satsuki and Mei's house and the hilltop antique shop from Whisper of the Heart, built at full size.

data.name: History_Heron_Text
data.value: The film opens with no trailer, no stills and a single poster, and audiences walk in knowing almost nothing. A boy who has lost his mother in the war follows a talking heron into another world. In March 2024 it wins the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. Months earlier, Nippon Television had become Ghibli's parent company, securing the studio's future beyond its founders.

data.name: History_Palme_Text
data.value: At Cannes, Studio Ghibli receives an honorary Palme d'Or, the first ever given to a studio rather than a person. Almost forty years after a rented floor in Kichijoji, the wind they wanted to blow through animation has reached the whole world.

data.name: FilmsIntro
data.value: Every feature Studio Ghibli has released, from Nausicaä to the most recent Oscar. Read them one by one in the detailed list, or switch to a wall of posters, and sort by release date or by what critics and audiences thought of each film.

data.name: FilmsShowRelated
data.value: Show films by the founders outside the studio

data.name: FilmsSectionRelatedIntro
data.value: Films that Miyazaki and Takahata worked on before the studio existed. They are not Ghibli productions, but a lot of what Ghibli became started here.

data.name: FilmsNausicaaNote
data.value: Made in 1984 at Topcraft, a year before Studio Ghibli existed. It is not technically a Ghibli production, but the studio counts it as the beginning of its story.

data.name: Film_Nausicaa_Title
data.value: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind

data.name: Film_Nausicaa_Synopsis
data.value: A thousand years after a war that poisoned the planet, a young princess tries to understand the toxic forest and the giant insects that everyone else only wants to burn. An ecological epic that paved the way for the studio.

data.name: Film_Laputa_Synopsis
data.value: Pazu, a boy from a mining town, sees a girl float down from the sky, and the two end up chased by pirates and soldiers who all want the same thing: the flying island of Laputa.

data.name: Film_GraveOfTheFireflies_Synopsis
data.value: In the last months of the war, two siblings who lost their home in the bombing of Kobe try to survive on their own. One of the most devastating animated films ever made, and one of the most tender.

data.name: Film_MyNeighborTotoro_Synopsis
data.value: Two sisters move to the countryside with their father while their mother recovers in a hospital nearby, and discover that the forest next to the house is full of spirits. No villain, no danger, just the feeling of being a child in summer.

data.name: Film_KikiDeliveryService_Synopsis
data.value: At thirteen, Kiki leaves home to spend a year living alone in a seaside town, as every young witch must, and starts a delivery service on her broomstick. A film about independence, work and the days when your magic just won't show up.

data.name: Film_OnlyYesterday_Synopsis
data.value: Taeko, a 27-year-old office worker from Tokyo, takes a trip to the countryside to help with the safflower harvest and keeps being visited by memories of when she was ten. Quiet, adult and surprisingly funny.

data.name: Film_PorcoRosso_Synopsis
data.value: Over the Adriatic in the 1920s, a World War I ace who was somehow turned into a pig hunts sky pirates for money and tries not to think about the past. Miyazaki's most relaxed film, full of seaplanes and old regrets.

data.name: Film_OceanWaves_Synopsis
data.value: A TV film made by the studio's younger staff: a college student remembers the transfer student from Tokyo who turned his last year of high school in Kochi upside down.

data.name: Film_PomPoko_Synopsis
data.value: The tanuki of the Tama Hills use every shape-shifting trick they know to stop a housing project from swallowing their forest. Funny, chaotic and, in the end, very sad.

data.name: Film_WhisperOfTheHeart_Synopsis
data.value: Shizuku, a girl who reads all the time, notices the same name on the library cards of every book she borrows. Following that clue leads her to an antique shop, a cat figurine and a boy who wants to make violins.

data.name: Film_PrincessMononoke_Synopsis
data.value: Cursed after defending his village from a raging boar god, the young prince Ashitaka travels west and ends up in the middle of a war between an iron-making town and the gods of the forest. Nobody here is simply right.

data.name: Film_MyNeighborsTheYamadas_Synopsis
data.value: Short watercolor sketches about the Yamadas, an ordinary family that forgets things, bickers, loses their daughter at the mall and still gets along. Takahata's gentlest film.

data.name: Film_SpiritedAway_Synopsis
data.value: On the way to their new home, ten-year-old Chihiro and her parents wander into a world of spirits. Her parents are turned into pigs, and she has to work in a bathhouse for the gods until she finds a way back.

data.name: Film_TheCatReturns_Synopsis
data.value: Haru saves a cat from being run over, and it turns out to be a prince. The Cat Kingdom's gratitude quickly becomes a problem when they decide she should marry him.

data.name: Film_HowlsMovingCastle_Synopsis
data.value: Sophie, a shy young hatter, is turned into an old woman by a witch's curse and finds shelter in the walking castle of Howl, a vain and famous wizard, while a war rages in the background.

data.name: Film_TalesFromEarthsea_Synopsis
data.value: In a land where dragons have started to reappear and magic is fading, the wizard Sparrowhawk travels with Arren, a troubled young prince running from something he did.

data.name: Film_Ponyo_Synopsis
data.value: A goldfish princess escapes from the sea, meets five-year-old Sosuke and decides she wants to be human, which throws the whole ocean off balance. Drawn almost entirely by hand.

data.name: Film_Arrietty_Synopsis
data.value: Arrietty belongs to a family of tiny people who live under the floorboards of a country house and borrow what they need from the humans upstairs. Everything changes when a sick boy staying in the house sees her.

data.name: Film_FromUpOnPoppyHill_Synopsis
data.value: Yokohama, 1963, a year before the Olympics. Umi, who raises signal flags every morning for her father lost at sea, joins a group of students fighting to save their old clubhouse from demolition.

data.name: Film_TheWindRises_Synopsis
data.value: A fictionalized life of Jiro Horikoshi, the engineer who dreamed of beautiful airplanes and designed the Zero fighter used in the war. Miyazaki's most personal film.

data.name: Film_TheTaleOfThePrincessKaguya_Title
data.value: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya

data.name: Film_TheTaleOfThePrincessKaguya_Synopsis
data.value: A bamboo cutter finds a tiny girl inside a glowing stalk and decides to raise her as a noble princess, whether she wants it or not. Takahata's last film, drawn in charcoal and watercolor.

data.name: Film_WhenMarnieWasThere_Synopsis
data.value: Anna, a lonely girl sent to spend the summer by the sea, becomes friends with Marnie, a mysterious blonde girl who lives in the old mansion across the marsh.

data.name: Film_TheRedTurtle_Synopsis
data.value: A man shipwrecked on a desert island tries again and again to escape, until a giant red turtle changes his plans. A co-production with Dutch director Michaël Dudok de Wit, told without a single word.

data.name: Film_EarwigAndTheWitch_Synopsis
data.value: Earwig, a sharp orphan who always manages to get her way, is adopted by a witch who only wants an extra pair of hands. The studio's first fully 3D film.

data.name: Film_TheBoyAndTheHeron_Synopsis
data.value: After losing his mother in a fire during the war, Mahito moves to the countryside, where a talking grey heron insists that she is still alive and leads him into another world.

data.name: Film_Horus_Synopsis
data.value: A boy with a sword of the sun returns to his father's homeland to protect a fishing village from an ice demon. Takahata's first feature, made at Toei with Miyazaki and Yasuo Otsuka.

data.name: Film_PussInBoots_Title
data.value: The Wonderful World of Puss 'n Boots

data.name: Film_PussInBoots_Synopsis
data.value: Pero, a cat on the run from the feline authorities for saving a mouse, helps a poor miller's son win the heart of a princess. Miyazaki animated its famous chase across the castle rooftops.

data.name: Film_PandaGoPanda_Synopsis
data.value: While her grandmother is away, little Mimiko takes in a panda cub and his very large father. Directed by Takahata and written by Miyazaki, it holds the first seeds of Totoro.

data.name: Film_Cagliostro_Synopsis
data.value: The gentleman thief Lupin III follows a trail of counterfeit money to a tiny European country and ends up trying to rescue a princess from a count's castle. Miyazaki's first feature.

data.name: Film_ChieTheBrat_Synopsis
data.value: In a working-class neighborhood of Osaka, eleven-year-old Chie runs the family's grilled offal restaurant while her father gambles and picks fights. Takahata at his most down to earth.

data.name: Film_GaucheTheCellist_Synopsis
data.value: Gauche, the weakest cellist in a small town orchestra, gets nightly visits from animals who, each in their own odd way, teach him how to play. Based on a story by Kenji Miyazawa.

data.name: Film_Yanagawa_Synopsis
data.value: A live-action documentary about a town in Kyushu that decided to save its old network of canals. Produced by Miyazaki with money from Nausicaä and directed with enormous patience by Takahata.

data.name: MeIntro1
data.value: Hi, I'm João Vitor Ventura, but most people just call me Ventura. I'm a .NET developer from Santa Catarina, Brazil, with about three years of experience building web and cross-platform applications, mostly with ASP.NET Core, Blazor and SQL Server.

data.name: MeIntro2
data.value: Before code, I studied chemistry at a technical high school and spent a semester in a lab working on a research project. Since then I've taken part in game jams, taught programming and worked as a freelancer, and each of those left something in the way I work: patience to explain, curiosity to test, and attention to the details that make software feel finished.

data.name: MeHow1Text
data.value: A year teaching beginners taught me to explain technical decisions without hiding behind jargon. The people I work with understand what was done and why.

data.name: MeHow2Title
data.value: I stay for the long run

data.name: MeHow2Text
data.value: Most of my freelance work comes from one long contract, more than a thousand hours on the same system. I know what it means to maintain code, not just to write it.

data.name: MeHow3Text
data.value: Unit and integration tests against real databases, and a good amount of time reading production logs. Having started in a lab probably helps.

data.name: StackIntro
data.value: The tools I work with, split by how well I really know them. I'd rather be clear about the difference between what I've shipped to production and what I'm still learning.

data.name: StackSiteIntro
data.value: This tribute is a hand-made project, designed by me in Figma and built without templates. Under the hood:

data.name: StackSite1
data.value: Blazor Server on .NET 8, with interactive server rendering and prerendering.

data.name: StackSite2
data.value: Tailwind CSS 4 with a custom theme for the Ghibli palette and fonts.

data.name: StackSite3
data.value: English and Portuguese through .resx files and ASP.NET Core localization, chosen by cookie.

data.name: StackSite4
data.value: Light, dark and system themes through JS interop and localStorage, applied before the first paint.

data.name: StackSite5
data.value: Posters from the Studio Ghibli API and ratings from the OMDb API, through typed HttpClients and an in-memory cache.

data.name: StackSite6
data.value: All texts, including the studio's history and the film synopses, written for this site.

data.name: Me_Chemistry_Text
data.value: I studied chemistry at IFSC, the Federal Institute of Santa Catarina. In my last year I joined Sustembalagem, a research project making water-resistant recycled paper for washing powder packages donated to vulnerable communities. We took the paper's water resistance from under a second to more than an hour.

data.name: Me_FirstCode_Text
data.value: My first program was Dark Dungeon Quest, a turn-based RPG in Python that ran in the terminal with ASCII art. Soon after came games in GameMaker, including a platformer built in less than a week for a game jam.

data.name: Me_College_Text
data.value: I graduated in Systems Analysis and Development at Senac Santa Catarina, working with C#, Java, Python and JavaScript, relational and non-relational databases, and deployments to the cloud.

data.name: Me_Paper_Text
data.value: I co-authored a paper proposing real-time bus routes integrated with Google Maps for rural communities, published in the journal REASE.

data.name: Me_Teacher_Text
data.value: For a year I taught people with no background in technology how to build for the web: ASP.NET Core, React, Blazor, SQL Server and Azure, in a full-stack course and in a front-end one. At the end of the course, my students were hosting their own databases in the cloud.

data.name: Me_Lume_Text
data.value: A college project I created: a movie recommendation app with a .NET MAUI client, an ASP.NET Core API and ML.NET clustering, with MySQL hosted on Azure.

data.name: Me_Freelance_Text
data.value: Since March 2025 I work as a freelancer, mostly on a long contract with an e-commerce and ERP company: ASP.NET Core and Blazor applications, SQL Server, custom Odoo modules, Shopify and shipping integrations, and the less glamorous part too, deploying to Windows Server and fixing what breaks in production.

data.name: Me_Now_Text
data.value: These days I'm building a history guessing game with Next.js and TypeScript on top of an ASP.NET Core API, and finally finishing this tribute to Studio Ghibli.

data.name: FiguresIntro
data.value: Studio Ghibli is usually told as the story of two directors, but a lot of people made it what it is: the founders, the artists who spent decades inside the studio, and friends, mentors and collaborators from outside it.

data.name: Figure_HayaoMiyazaki_Bio
data.value: The director most people think of when they hear the name Ghibli. He started as an in-between animator at Toei in 1963 and has directed twelve features, drawing an obsession with flight, strong young heroines and the natural world into almost all of them. He has announced his retirement more than once, and came back every time.

data.name: Figure_HayaoMiyazaki_Works
data.value: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind;My Neighbor Totoro;Princess Mononoke;Spirited Away;The Boy and the Heron

data.name: Figure_IsaoTakahata_Bio
data.value: Five years older than Miyazaki, and the one who taught him that animation could be serious. A reader of French poetry who took years to finish each film, he never repeated a visual style: realism in Grave of the Fireflies, comic strip in the Yamadas, charcoal sketches in Kaguya. He also produced Nausicaä and Castle in the Sky.

data.name: Figure_IsaoTakahata_Works
data.value: Heidi;Grave of the Fireflies;Only Yesterday;Pom Poko;The Tale of the Princess Kaguya

data.name: Figure_ToshioSuzuki_Bio
data.value: An editor at Animage magazine who wouldn't take no for an answer from either director, and ended up becoming the producer who kept the studio alive. He found ways to finance films nobody wanted to fund, sold Totoro and Grave of the Fireflies as a double feature, and ran the studio as president after it became independent.

data.name: Figure_YasuyoshiTokuma_Bio
data.value: The founder of the publisher Tokuma Shoten, a businessman with a gambler's instinct who also ran the film studio Daiei. He trusted Suzuki, and Suzuki trusted Miyazaki and Takahata: his money made the Nausicaä film possible and, a year later, a studio. He stayed behind Ghibli as executive producer until his death.

data.name: Figure_YasuyoshiTokuma_Works
data.value: Tokuma Shoten;Executive producer of Ghibli films

data.name: Figure_YoshifumiKondo_Bio
data.value: For many at the studio, the natural successor. He was the character designer of Takahata's Anne of Green Gables, animation director of Grave of the Fireflies and Only Yesterday, and directed Whisper of the Heart in 1995. He died in 1998, at 47, and it remains his only film as director.

data.name: Figure_YoshifumiKondo_Works
data.value: Whisper of the Heart;Grave of the Fireflies;Only Yesterday

data.name: Figure_MichiyoYasuda_Bio
data.value: She met Takahata and Miyazaki at Toei and chose the colors of their films for more than three decades, from Nausicaä to The Wind Rises. The soft greens of Totoro and the glowing night of Spirited Away's bathhouse passed through her hands.

data.name: Figure_MichiyoYasuda_Works
data.value: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind;My Neighbor Totoro;Spirited Away;The Wind Rises

data.name: Figure_KazuoOga_Bio
data.value: The painter behind the forests people remember. As art director of My Neighbor Totoro he gave the Japanese countryside its most famous portrait, and he went on to lead the backgrounds of Only Yesterday, Pom Poko and Princess Mononoke.

data.name: Figure_KazuoOga_Works
data.value: My Neighbor Totoro;Only Yesterday;Pom Poko;Princess Mononoke

data.name: Figure_GoroMiyazaki_Bio
data.value: Hayao's son trained as a landscape designer and first came to the studio to run the Ghibli Museum. He then directed Tales from Earthsea, against his father's wishes, followed by From Up on Poppy Hill and Earwig and the Witch, and led the creation of Ghibli Park.

data.name: Figure_GoroMiyazaki_Works
data.value: Tales from Earthsea;From Up on Poppy Hill;Earwig and the Witch;Ghibli Park

data.name: Figure_HiromasaYonebayashi_Bio
data.value: An animator who grew up inside the studio and directed Arrietty and When Marnie Was There. When Ghibli paused production in 2014, he left with producer Yoshiaki Nishimura to help found Studio Ponoc.

data.name: Figure_YasuoOtsuka_Bio
data.value: One of Toei's first animators and the teacher of both founders. A lover of jeeps and anything with an engine, he was animation director of Takahata's first feature and of Miyazaki's, and spent his later years training new animators.

data.name: Figure_YasuoOtsuka_Works
data.value: Horus, Prince of the Sun;The Castle of Cagliostro;Lupin III

data.name: Figure_PaulGrimault_Bio
data.value: His film The Shepherdess and the Chimney Sweep showed a young Takahata that animation could be poetic and political at once. Decades later, Ghibli helped bring the finished version, The King and the Mockingbird, to Japanese theaters.

data.name: Figure_JoeHisaishi_Bio
data.value: He met Miyazaki on Nausicaä and has scored every one of his features since, as well as Takahata's Kaguya. It is hard to think of Totoro, Mononoke or Spirited Away without hearing his music.

data.name: Figure_JoeHisaishi_Works
data.value: My Neighbor Totoro;Princess Mononoke;Spirited Away;Howl's Moving Castle

data.name: Figure_JohnLasseter_Bio
data.value: A friend of Miyazaki since the early eighties and one of the loudest defenders of Ghibli in the United States. He oversaw the English version of Spirited Away, the film that introduced the studio to many Western audiences.

data.name: Figure_JohnLasseter_Works
data.value: Toy Story;English version of Spirited Away

data.name: Figure_HideakiAnno_Bio
data.value: As a young animator he drew the God Warrior scene in Nausicaä, and went on to create Neon Genesis Evangelion. Miyazaki later cast him as the voice of Jiro, the engineer at the center of The Wind Rises.

data.name: Figure_HideakiAnno_Works
data.value: Neon Genesis Evangelion;Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind;The Wind Rises

data.name: Figure_MichaelDudokDeWit_Bio
data.value: A Dutch animator whose Oscar-winning short Father and Daughter caught the studio's attention. Ghibli invited him to make his first feature with them, The Red Turtle, a film without a single line of dialogue.

data.name: Figure_DianaWynneJones_Bio
data.value: The British author of the novel that became Howl's Moving Castle. Her last book, Earwig and the Witch, became the studio's first fully 3D film, directed by Goro Miyazaki.

data.name: Figure_DianaWynneJones_Works
data.value: Howl's Moving Castle;Earwig and the Witch
